Share in-memory acquisition, pending requests and revisions across configured compatible tabs while keeping per-tab UI state separate. Closing one tab must not break others. Reopening after all tabs close may reacquire data; durable frontend data remains distinct.

Implementation progress: a configured SharedWorker now owns the frontend engine, HTTP connections and acquisition/evaluation caches. Each tab keeps a rendering mirror and independent UI state. The tab configuration still permits separate engines. Browser recording shared-engine-ui.spec.ts proves shared identity, cross-tab acquired-node visibility, one owner evaluation for unchanged reads, independent acquisition in isolated mode, and survival when one shared tab closes. Remaining verification: full graph consumer refresh, bounded data freshness across mirrored routes, restart identity and lifecycle cleanup. No persisted cache was added.

Further verification: Activity board acquisition/retention, graph manual and automatic refresh, and compatible/isolated-tab sharing pass together (3 browser tests). The worker is the single acquisition owner; rendering mirrors no longer retain a competing operation snapshot. Service engine identities are unique per runtime, observed connections are engine-owned graph edges, and the startup generation separates worker sharing after a service restart. The deterministic application boundary scan reports zero current bypasses; its negative fixtures still fail as expected. Full completion remains gated by composition, consumer freshness coverage, and checkpoint verification.

Four shared-engine browser tests now pass, covering configured frontend contributors, shared/isolated acquisition ownership, and connections to an additional service by explicit URL. Local credentials are not forwarded. Test synchronization is being migrated from obsolete domain routes and network-idle waits to actual engine operations and request lifecycle events.

Slice verification completed: Four browser recordings verify configured local contributors, compatible-tab sharing, isolated-tab configuration, a surviving tab, deduplicated unchanged reads, and explicit remote connections. No persisted materialization cache was introduced.
properties.title: Share compatible frontend engines across tabs
